# Building and extending Blue 3

Blue 3 is a TypeScript monorepo with an Electron application, a
platform-neutral `@blue/data` project model, a Java-runtime helper,
and a native Blue Engine. The archived Java manual's Maven and
NetBeans-module instructions apply to the older application, not this
repository.

Install Node.js 22 or newer and pnpm 12.8.1, matching the repository's
`packageManager` version and CI setup. App source builds also
need Java 17 or newer, Maven 3 or newer, CMake 3.21 or newer, and a C/C++
toolchain. The native build bootstraps the repository's pinned vcpkg revision.
Install Quarto to build the manual. Csound 7 is required for playback and
rendering; it is not required to open and edit projects.

On macOS, the C/C++ toolchain comes from Xcode or the Xcode Command Line
Tools. Check that `xcode-select -p` identifies the installed toolchain.

## Build from a fresh checkout

After installing the prerequisites, run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kunstmusik/blue.git
cd blue
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm lint
pnpm --filter @blue/app manual:build
pnpm --filter @blue/app start
```

The first build downloads and bootstraps the pinned vcpkg checkout and
builds its native dependencies. Maven also downloads the Java helper's
dependencies. Allow network access and extra time for this first build.
The final command opens the built Electron app. For development with
automatic reload after edits, use `pnpm --filter @blue/app dev` instead.

To create and verify an unsigned local application package after building:

```bash
pnpm --filter @blue/app package:dir
pnpm --filter @blue/app verify:packaged-app
```

The packaging command rebuilds and bundles the manual. For changes limited
to the application, the package scripts under `packages/blue-app` offer
more focused validation. The manual can also be built directly with
`quarto render docs/manual --to html`.

## Extension boundaries

Start in `packages/blue-data` for project models, XML compatibility,
note generation, and CSD policy. Host filesystem, processes, the engine,
and Java runtime integration belong in the Electron main process or
their host packages. Renderer work uses typed preload and IPC contracts.
Read the repository's `AGENTS.md`, `docs/modularization.md`, and
`.specify/memory/constitution.md` before changing those boundaries.

Blue 3 does not expose the Java application's NetBeans RCP plugin APIs.
When extending a SoundObject, instrument, Note Processor, or widget, follow
the extension type's model registration and serialization paths, its editor
contract, and the ProjectHistory path for user edits. Extend CSD generation
or note processing where that feature requires it. Preserve unknown `.blue`
data and compare Java behavior for compatibility changes. Feature-specific
requirements and validation belong in `specs/`.
